text:
Josh Doan's goal against Columbus on Friday came with a reporter's aside attached: Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon wrote that "all the haters" were "eating crow tonight." That tells you the mood. Doan has 4 points in 16 games, his ice time is down more than a minute from his usual, and he played 11:42 in that win.

The frustrating part is how good he was last season. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.2 wins above replacement, 42nd among 401 forwards, and his adjusted impact on chance creation ranked in the 97th percentile. This year Buffalo takes only 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, more than six points worse than without him. That gap is the real concern, more than the points.

His own shooting is close to fine: 3 goals on 3.98 expected. His points rate is 0.98 per 60 against a talent range we put between 1.7 and 2.5, which is why our projection still says about 39 points. He's 24, fast (93rd percentile top speed), and still finding his place behind Buffalo's top six. We'd give him time.
headline: Josh Doan and the patience test
